title: The Half Life of Agent Infrastructure — Ben Kus, Box
talk_summary: Box CTO Ben Kus argues that AI agent infrastructure has a half-life measured in months, not years, so the winning strategy is to 'get good at changing' rather than betting on any single stack. He gives three concrete mechanisms: abstraction layers that let you swap components, eval sets as the gate for any switch, and evaluating vendors on their track record of handling change.

takeaways.what_they_do: Before adopting any new model/agent approach, they run it against a fixed eval set of same-input/expected-output cases graded on cost, speed, quality, and capability; only switch if it wins on what customers care about.
takeaways.evidence_quote: Does the new approach work better for our eval sets? What the customer cares about? If the answer is yes, strongly consider switching.

takeaways.technique: Adaptive model selection as the current best practice
takeaways.what_they_do: Instead of one frontier model or self-hosted open weights, pick big vs small models per task based on which does well.
takeaways.evidence_quote: nowadays is probably the best approach is to do an adaptive model selection where you basically are picking the big and smaller models

takeaways.what_they_do: Box has an agent abstraction so they can swap the underlying approach (graph → loop → skills → sandbox) while the customer-facing agent behavior stays the same.
takeaways.evidence_quote: whenever possible if you can build an abstraction so that it lets you swap out what's underneath

takeaways.what_they_do: They review every AI technology choice every six months regardless of satisfaction, versus three years for other infra.
takeaways.evidence_quote: at Box we are now in the habit of reviewing every six months no matter what
takeaways.numbers: 6-month review cadence vs 3 years for other infra

takeaways.technique: Vendor selection by change-handling track record
takeaways.what_they_do: When picking platforms, they look at how the vendor handled the last 6-12 months of transitions, not just current features and roadmap.
takeaways.evidence_quote: look back how have they handled change what's their attitude towards change
